result.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
result.summary: Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanning quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning domains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail our integrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「Into the Unknown」基准：让 9 个前沿 agent 各就 DOE 国家实验室科学家提供的未发表后续研究方向写出 15 篇后续论文，以科学家给出的条件构成 rubric 进行评估，结果 135 篇无一满足全部条件，114 篇未通过完整性检查。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「完整性检查」关注产出是否声称未做的工作、数字是否与记录证据矛盾，可能为核查推理输出是否真实使用内部或视觉证据、以及在无参考答案情形下设计评估标准提供借鉴线索，属较远领域，需人工核查。
